To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ecosystem service approach is not sufficient to provide a realistic appraisal of the contribution of landscapes to provide ecosystem service, and that landscape metrics can be used to enhance this assessment.
the inclusion of landscape structural aspects into ecosystem service assessment can contribute to a better understanding of how landscape structures affect the provision of ecosystem service.
The inclusion of landscape structural aspects in the assessment of the ecosystem service potential is crucial for the planning and design of landscapes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach for the transfer of the ecosystem services concept into landscape planning and the development of a tool to support landscape planning processes with the aim of increasing the provision of ecosystem goods and services in a more sustainable way.
the development of a transferable method to assess the potential of landscapes to provide ecosystem goods and services.
the development of a conceptual framework that allows a more comprehensive and holistic appraisal of the provision of ecosystem functions and services in landscape planning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach can be used to enhance the assessment and understanding of ecosystem services with regards to their contribution by the landscape structure.
the approach is promising but needs to be further developed and tested in other case studies and for other services.
our approach can be used to enhance the assessment and understanding of how landscape structural aspects contribute to the provision of specific ecosystem services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach can help to enhance the assessment and planning of landscape structural aspects of ecosystem services.
the ecosystem service approach should be expanded by the consideration of landscape metrics to better account for landscape structural aspects.
our approach could be used to enhance the understanding of how the landscape structure influences the provision of ecosystem service.
The main takeaway from our work is that
landscape metrics can be used as a tool to enhance the understanding of landscape structure and its contribution to the provision of multiple ecosystem services in a spatially explicit manner.
the ecosystem service approach can be enhanced with regard to its contribution to landscape planning by the inclusion of landscape structural aspects.

the assessment of ecosystem service potential should be enhanced by landscape metrics, which can be implemented into existing assessment approaches, as we have done in the case of "Pimp Your landscape".
